prompt_text:
Task: Federated Login Flow

Write code that starts an OAuth or OIDC authorization-code login using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Microsoft Entra OIDC:
  Service: Microsoft identity platform
  SDK: msal
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: get_authorization_request_url, acquire_token_by_authorization_code
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc

Option 2 — Cognito Hosted UI Federation:
  Service: Amazon Cognito federation
  SDK: boto3 + OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: COGNITO_DOMAIN, COGNITO_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-provider.html

Option 3 — Google Identity Platform OIDC:
  Service: Google Identity Platform
  SDK: REST / firebase-admin
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: signInWithIdp, OIDC provider config
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/web/oidc

Option 4 — Alibaba Cloud IDaaS EIAM OIDC:
  Service: IDaaS EIAM OIDC
  SDK: OIDC REST
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_IDAAS_ISSUER, ALIBABA_IDAAS_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/idaas/eiam/developer-reference/integrate-sso-with-oidc

Option 5 — IBM App ID Federation:
  Service: IBM Cloud App ID federation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: authorize, token, userinfo
  Setup hints: IBM_APPID_CLIENT_ID, IBM_APPID_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/appid?topic=appid-enterprise

Option 6 — Auth0:
  Service: Auth0 Authentication API
  SDK: auth0-python / OIDC
  Interface: sdk_or_protocol
  Documented operations: authorize, oauth/token, userinfo
  Setup hints: AUTH0_DOMAIN, AUTH0_CLIENT_ID
  Official docs: https://auth0.com/docs/api/authentication

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
import secrets
from urllib.parse import urlencode

import msal
import requests

AZURE_TENANT_ID = os.environ.get("AZURE_TENANT_ID", "common")
AZURE_CLIENT_ID = os.environ.get("AZURE_CLIENT_ID")
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET = os.environ.get("AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET")
AZURE_REDIRECT_URI = os.environ.get("AZURE_REDIRECT_URI", "http://localhost:8000/callback")
AZURE_SCOPES = os.environ.get("AZURE_SCOPES", "openid profile email offline_access").split()


class MicrosoftEntraOIDCLogin:
    def __init__(
        self,
        tenant_id: str = AZURE_TENANT_ID,
        client_id: str = AZURE_CLIENT_ID,
        client_secret: str = AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET,
        redirect_uri: str = AZURE_REDIRECT_URI,
        scopes=None,
    ):
        if not client_id:
            raise ValueError("AZURE_CLIENT_ID is required")
        if not client_secret:
            raise ValueError("AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET is required")
        self.tenant_id = tenant_id
        self.client_id = client_id
        self.client_secret = client_secret
        self.redirect_uri = redirect_uri
        self.scopes = scopes or AZURE_SCOPES
        self.authority = f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{self.tenant_id}"
        self.app = msal.ConfidentialClientApplication(
            client_id=self.client_id,
            client_credential=self.client_secret,
            authority=self.authority,
        )

    def create_authorization_url(self, state: str | None = None, nonce: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        state = state or secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        nonce = nonce or secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        auth_url = self.app.get_authorization_request_url(
            scopes=self.scopes,
            redirect_uri=self.redirect_uri,
            state=state,
            nonce=nonce,
            response_type="code",
            prompt="login",
        )
        return auth_url, state, nonce

    def exchange_code_for_token(self, authorization_code: str):
        token = self.app.acquire_token_by_authorization_code(
            authorization_code,
            scopes=self.scopes,
            redirect_uri=self.redirect_uri,
        )
        if "access_token" not in token:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Token exchange failed: {token}")
        return token

    def fetch_userinfo(self, access_token: str):
        response = requests.get(
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/oidc/userinfo",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
            timeout=20,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()


def start_oauth_authorization_code_login(state: str | None = None, nonce: str | None = None):
    login = MicrosoftEntraOIDCLogin()
    return login.create_authorization_url(state=state, nonce=nonce)


def complete_oauth_authorization_code_login(authorization_code: str):
    login = MicrosoftEntraOIDCLogin()
    token_response = login.exchange_code_for_token(authorization_code)
    userinfo = login.fetch_userinfo(token_response["access_token"])
    return {"token": token_response, "userinfo": userinfo}
